markdown_report:
**Selected experiment.** Retain the lexical residual inside the corrected HSTU, but replace the underspecified history-conditioned input gate with a shared item-side gate. This reduces implementation risk at 0% progress; benefits remain unmeasured.

**Insights and framework.** Three starting insights guide the proposal. (1) Users reject broad associations and missed function/format distinctions. Text could expose finer evidence, but cannot verify compatibility. (2) Recent purchases can represent completed needs. Histories cannot establish completion, so redundancy reduction remains exploratory. (3) Electronics has 10.71% sampled wrong ranks and a −0.0749 lower-decile margin. Collapse scores near 0.5 do not justify collapse regularization.

Three literature insights refine implementation. (1) [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152) already provides feature gating. Preserve its backbone and avoid duplicating mechanisms without evidence. (2) [HLLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12740) motivates jointly learned text representations. Its architecture and initialization results do not validate this lightweight adaptation. (3) [Semantic fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) cautions against direct embedding addition. A projected residual with baseline-preserving initialization is therefore a testable design choice, not an established remedy.

| Direction | Mechanism | Addressed gap |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | Multi-negative softmax | Confusing candidates |
| Temporal conditioning | Historical contribution gate | Stale demand |
| Representation | Gated lexical residual | Specific function/content |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each dimension includes benefit (+) and limitation (−).

- **128-negative softmax: 2/7/4/9/2.** Originality: +HSTU precedent, −established; potential: +discrimination, −false negatives; user: +finer ranking, −no compatibility evidence; model: +Electronics confusion, −easy-margin shortcuts; difficulty: +small change, −temperature tuning. Reference: [official configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin).
- **Recency gate: 4/7/8/5/5.** Originality: +contextual timing, −existing bias; potential: +adaptive relevance, −completion unobserved; user: +current purpose, −repeat demand varies; model: +context discrimination, −weak diagnostic support; difficulty: +compact layer, −timestamp alignment. Reference: HSTU.
- **Lexical residual: 3/7/8/7/4.** Originality: +constrained integration, −established fusion; potential: +shared distinctions, −missing text; user: +function/format evidence, −compatibility uncertain; model: +Electronics discrimination, −superficial shortcuts; difficulty: +small encoder, −serialization and scoring consistency. References: HLLM, AttrFormer, semantic fusion.

**Chosen method.** Pool randomly initialized title/description token embeddings, project them, and apply a learned item gate plus zero-initialized residual scaling. Share the resulting item representation between causal HSTU inputs and candidate scoring. Keep the baseline objective, optimizer, and sampler.

This addresses broad thematic matching and overlooked connector/format distinctions; Electronics separation supplies the model-facing target. Preserve one checkpoint/category, final-nonpadding readout, diagnostic interfaces, seeds, routing, and training limits.

Select by pinned sampled macro validation HR@10. Compare ID-only and lexical models first; defer title/description, gate, and dropout ablations. Inspect frequency, text availability, title overlap, and norm/popularity associations; shuffled-text controls can probe shortcuts. Paired within-category user bootstrap intervals describe conditional uncertainty, not repeated-selection bias. One additional hit changes macro HR by 0.00125. Sampled HR does not establish full-catalog quality or verified compatibility.

idea.description: Add a compact, jointly trained lexical residual to the supplied corrected HSTU. Encode public training-item titles and descriptions using randomly initialized token embeddings, pool and project the text, and incorporate it through a shared item-side gate with zero-initialized residual scaling. Use the same item representation for sequence inputs and candidate scoring. Train exactly one model per category.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies overly broad thematic recommendations and overlooked connector, format, dimension, and content distinctions. These are two explicit user-facing targets for lexical features. Electronics supplies the quantitative target: its sampled wrong-rank rate is 10.71%, its lower-decile margin is −0.0749, and 16.36% of margins fall below 0.5. Text may improve discrimination, but matching words does not establish physical compatibility, immediate usefulness, or fulfilled needs. Collapse scores near 0.5 indicate approximately zero mean pairwise cosine similarity and do not support adding collapse regularization. At 0% progress, retain this feasible representation experiment; multi-negative softmax remains a strong subsequent alternative rather than an additional simultaneous change.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected HSTU blocks, causal attention, baseline loss, optimizer, sampler, split logic, and checkpoint-selection schedule. Replace the previous proposal's underspecified history-conditioned input gate with a shared item-side gate; keep temporal conditioning as a separate future experiment. The revised gate introduces no recurrent dependency or target conditioning.

Use only supplied public titles/descriptions for items appearing in training histories. Build vocabulary independently per category, without validation/test interaction information. Normalize text with Unicode NFKC and lowercase; tokenize with an explicit deterministic pattern preserving alphanumeric identifiers and internal hyphens, periods, and slashes, for example [a-z0-9]+(?:[-./][a-z0-9]+)*. Reserve padding and unknown IDs. Keep tokens with training-catalog document frequency at least two, cap vocabulary at 20,000 including reserved tokens, and break frequency ties lexicographically. Encode up to 32 title tokens and 32 description tokens separately. Use a shared 32-dimensional token embedding initialized from scratch; masked-mean pool each field, concatenate the two vectors, and apply one bias-free linear projection to the baseline item dimension. Empty fields pool to zero. Items without usable text receive an exactly zero text residual.

Define z_i = e_i + alpha * sigmoid(w^T e_i + b) * P(text_i). Initialize alpha to zero, b to −2, and other new parameters with ordinary seeded random initialization. This reproduces the baseline item representation initially, while allowing alpha to learn before the initially inactive text branch receives task gradients. Use whole-item text dropout with probability 0.1 during training, shared across repeated occurrences of an item within the batch; disable it at inference. Padding representations must remain zero. Preserve baseline positional embeddings, normalization, relative biases, and HSTU feature gating after constructing z_i. Do not add cosine normalization or temperature changes in this experiment. Use z_i for both sequence embedding lookup and candidate scoring, retaining any existing baseline scoring transformations. No separately fitted text scores or auxiliary predictors are permitted.

Maintain item_emb as the actual ID embedding module, log2feats(sequence) as the causal HSTU feature interface, and predict_score(features, items) as the canonical scorer incorporating candidate lexical residuals. Preserve the host's broadcasting and output-shape conventions. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Diagnostics must call predict_score rather than reconstruct scores from item_emb alone. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and definitions. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Label ID-embedding collapse explicitly as an ID-only statistic; optionally report effective-representation cosine and norm statistics separately. Do not infer missing category breakdowns, review properties, or simulator traits.

Read inference features using the maximum index where sequence != 0, never count minus one. Preserve baseline handling of empty histories. Remask padded outputs and retain causal/key-padding masking. Verify that changing future tokens leaves earlier features unchanged in evaluation mode, that adding left padding preserves equivalent valid-position features under the baseline position convention, that padding contributes no lexical residual, and that checkpoint reload and generated predictor produce matching scores for identical inputs.

Save vocabulary, item token buffers, architecture configuration, and model weights beneath the trial directory. Include buffers and scalar alpha in the single model state. Update the embedded predictor writer with the identical architecture, deterministic token assets, and scoring path. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and 200 batches per epoch. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. Use a single GPU. Do not read other trials, reuse their checkpoints, obtain pretrained weights, or use unavailable reviews, ratings, prices, stores, or structured categories.

Compare the unchanged ID-only baseline with this one lexical configuration using the pinned evaluator: 200 validation users per category, one positive and 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42, macro-average HR@10. Keep evaluator candidate generation unchanged. Record all trials and checkpoint selections against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, including diagnostics and failures. Further title-only versus title-plus-description, fixed-addition versus gated-residual, and text-dropout ablations are sequential optional experiments only if budget remains; each uses one model/category and is never fused with another. Treat brand-like token masking as a heuristic control because verified brand annotations are unavailable. Item-text shuffling within training-popularity bins tests dependence on meaningful item-text alignment but does not isolate brand reliance by itself.

Supplement selection with Electronics margin diagnostics and descriptive validation breakdowns by training frequency, text availability, and title overlap. Report embedding-norm/training-popularity correlations as associations, not proof of popularity shortcuts. If existing evaluator outputs expose per-user hit indicators without altering the evaluator, bootstrap paired user differences within each category 2,000 times with diagnostic RNG seed 42, then average category differences equally. These intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates; they do not capture training randomness, candidate-sampling variability, or repeated-selection optimism. One additional hit changes a category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Do not claim held-out gains, full-catalog quality, reduced incompatibility, or reduced redundancy from sampled validation HR alone. Retain the native full-catalog unseen-item qualitative assessment for five real training users per category.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    baseline = supplied_corrected_hstu(category)
    vocab, title_ids, description_ids = tokenize_training_catalog_text(
        min_document_frequency=2, max_vocab=20000,
        max_title_tokens=32, max_description_tokens=32)
    model = HSTUWithLexicalResidual(
        baseline, vocab, title_ids, description_ids,
        token_dim=32, text_dropout=0.1, alpha_init=0.0,
        gate_bias_init=-2.0)

    # One jointly trained representation, shared by inputs and candidates:
    # title_i = masked_mean(token_embedding(title_ids[i]))
    # description_i = masked_mean(token_embedding(description_ids[i]))
    # text_i = bias_free_projection(concat(title_i, description_i))
    # gate_i = sigmoid(dot(gate_weight, item_emb(i)) + gate_bias)
    # z_i = item_emb(i) + alpha * gate_i * text_i
    # Empty text and padding have exactly zero text contribution.
    # During training, apply one whole-text dropout mask per distinct batch item.
    # log2feats uses z_sequence inside the unchanged causal HSTU.
    # predict_score uses z_candidates through the unchanged baseline score function.

    for epoch in range(configured_epochs_at_most_200):
        for batch in range(200):
            sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch()
            model.prepare_shared_batch_text_dropout(sequence, positive, negative)
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            positive_logits = model.predict_score(features, positive)
            negative_logits = model.predict_score(features, negative)
            loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(
                positive_logits, negative_logits, positive != 0)
            unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
        follow_unchanged_baseline_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()

    save_one_selected_checkpoint_with_all_text_assets(model)
    emit_matching_predictor_architecture_and_loading_code()
    verify_causality_padding_reload_and_predictor_score_consistency()

# Inference:
# valid_index = max(index where sequence != 0), with baseline empty-history handling
# features = model.log2feats(sequence)[batch_index, valid_index]
# scores = model.predict_score(features, candidate_items)

# Compare completed four-category trials using pinned sampled macro validation HR@10.
# Never combine predictions or checkpoints from different trials.

originality.positive: The shared lexical residual is a concrete adaptation to the corrected HSTU, its diagnostic contract, and the single-model restriction.
originality.negative: Text pooling, ID/text fusion, learned gates, and zero-initialized residual scaling are established techniques. The supplied evidence does not support claiming a new general recommendation method.

future_potential.positive: A small text branch could share specific function and content evidence across sparse item histories and provide a controlled foundation for subsequent temporal or objective experiments.
future_potential.negative: Randomly initialized mean pooling may learn weak semantics or popularity and lexical shortcuts. Missing descriptions and incomplete compatibility evidence limit the conclusions even if sampled HR improves.

code_difficulty.positive: A shared item gate avoids the previous history-conditioning ambiguity and requires no additional backbone, pretrained model, or independent scoring system.
code_difficulty.negative: Deterministic text assets, consistent batch text dropout, candidate scoring, diagnosis adapters, checkpoint loading, and embedded predictor generation still require careful integration. The exact baseline source is needed to produce a runnable patch.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU sequential transduction with feature gating and relative attention biases.
Provides the required backbone and explains why an additional context gate needs separate justification.
limitations: Does not establish gains from the proposed lexical residual on this Amazon benchmark.
Temporal and feature gates do not directly identify completed needs.

related_work.title: Official HSTU implementation
contributions: Documents HSTU projections, causal attention, multiplicative feature gating, and residual computation.
Provides architectural context for preserving the family.
limitations: The host-supplied corrected baseline remains the implementation authority for this experiment.
Does not validate the previously proposed shifted-context gate or this lexical adaptation.

related_work.title: HLLM: Enhancing Sequential Recommendations via Hierarchical Large Language Models for Item and User Modeling
contributions: Motivates learning item-text and user-sequence representations through recommendation supervision.
Includes training from scratch as discussed in the supplied search evidence.
limitations: Uses a different architecture and more expressive text modeling.
Its initialization comparisons and reported gains do not establish benefits from a randomly initialized mean-pooled HSTU text branch.

related_work.title: Learning Attribute-as-Explicit Relation for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates modeling specific attribute relations beyond undifferentiated item similarity.
limitations: Structured attributes are unavailable here.
Title and description tokens are incomplete proxies for attributes and compatibility.

related_work.title: Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion
contributions: The supplied search evidence identifies differences between text and ID representations as a reason direct addition can be ineffective.
Motivates controlled comparisons of projected and gated fusion.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed gate or zero-initialized scaling solves the mismatch in HSTU.
Its results cannot be transferred directly to this constrained from-scratch encoder.

related_work.title: TASTE
contributions: Reports recommendation improvements and reduced popularity bias through text matching in its evaluated setting.
limitations: Uses pretrained language models, which are unavailable under this task's initialization constraints.
Does not demonstrate equivalent gains from randomly initialized mean-pooled token embeddings.

related_work.title: NISER
contributions: Links embedding norms and popularity bias in session recommendation.
Motivates descriptive norm/popularity diagnostics.
limitations: Does not establish the same mechanism in the supplied HSTU.
Norm correlations alone do not identify causal shortcuts or justify changing normalization.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Provides precedent for zero-initialized trainable residual scaling.
Supports an initialization that preserves the baseline representation before learning.
limitations: Does not evaluate this item-text residual or establish recommendation gains.
At initialization, the text branch receives no task gradient until its residual scale moves away from zero.

related_work.title: Official HSTU sampled-softmax configuration
contributions: Supplies a practical precedent for 128 negatives, normalized embeddings, and temperature scaling.
Supports multi-negative softmax as a feasible alternative experiment.
limitations: These choices are not established optima for the four Amazon datasets.
Changing the objective simultaneously would obscure attribution of lexical-residual effects.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and reverse model orderings.
Supports describing the pinned selection measure explicitly as sampled validation HR@10.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the fixed evaluator.
Does not determine the direction or magnitude of sampling effects for these particular trials.

related_work.title: BPR: Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
contributions: Provides a pairwise positive-over-negative learning objective.
Helps distinguish training-margin improvement from crossing the evaluation rank-10 boundary.
limitations: Improved pairwise loss or margins do not guarantee higher sampled HR@10.
Does not supply compatibility or fulfilled-need supervision.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit finite validation data.
Motivates limiting exploratory comparisons and recording all selection decisions.
limitations: Fixed seeds do not remove selection optimism.
A paired user bootstrap does not correct repeated-selection bias.

related_work.title: Computing Confidence Intervals for Common IR Measures
contributions: Provides methodological support for uncertainty estimates around retrieval averages.
Motivates paired resampling of per-user outcomes for descriptive model comparisons.
limitations: The proposed bootstrap is conditional on fitted models and fixed candidate sets.
It does not quantify training randomness, negative-candidate variability, or selection-induced optimism.
